subject: Problem in combining F2 with F3 generation

messages.author: 7409d4321b2ec671
messages.subject: Problem in combining F2 with F3 generation
parts:
Dear Karl and R/qtl discussion group members,
This can be novice question but I am shamelessly asking it since I couldn't find an answer after puzzling for a while.
I have performed QTL mapping for an animal (fish) behavior using F2 and F3 generations with r/qtl and QTLRel. To Karl, thank you very much for your kind helpful advice in the other day!
The combining F2 with F3 sounds unusual but our idea was to gain further phenotypic variance as well as higher resolution by extra recombination events in order to yield higher statistical power in the limited time. I, of course, had a problem of the relatedness among F2 and F3 so that I ran QTL mapping under QTLRel environment to resolve this.
Then another problem came up when I compared the results of scanOne between with and without relatedness (= variance component) to see how they were different. Surprisingly, a lot of significant QTL peaks (over p=0.05 permutation threshold) in the “without relatedness”-QTL scan were gone in the “with relatedness”-QTL scan, suggesting that many of QTL peaks in the “without relatedness”-scan were the false positives. This can be true but, when I take a look at the plotPXG at a couple of fake QTLs, the most of F3 (not F2) were BB homozygotes and they drag the phenotype to the one direction (such as, if the behavior ranges 0.0 – 1.0 and the average of F2 is 0.5, many of F3, which have BB genotype, show ~1.0).  This can raise two different hypotheses: (1) “B” allele has a genuine effect to drag the behavioral phenotype toward 1.0, or (2) most of F3 phenotypes are ~1.0 so that wherever the genomic loci have skewed genotype ratio (such as AA:AB:BB are 0%:10%:90% in F3, respectively), the “high (~1.0)” phenotype is always associated with BB genotype at such loci if F3 individual number is large enough against F2.
I imagine QTLRel is for resolving these two hypotheses but I would like to perform multiple QTL mapping to control noise-variance and its too hard to perform it under QTLRel to me (because I must handle a lot of command functions without making mistakes or misunderstandings).
I would really appreciate it if anyone suggests and/or advices me alternative methods to separate above two hypotheses.
I saw multiple skewed-genotype loci since I have developed F3 through the marker-assisted selection of F2 parents. high (~1.0)-behavior. I successfully got F3 with high (~1.0)-behavioral scores and expected the skewed genotype around the marker region in these F3 but, with some unknown reason, I saw the skewed genotype in totally unlinked LG too. This fact motivates me to separate above two hypotheses to recover “genuine” QTLs.

I appreciate your time and kind thoughts in advance.
Thank you!

Masato

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problem in combining F2 with F3 generation
parts:
It's not so surprising that there would be significant peaks when you ignore relationships that would go away when you take account of relationships.

The reason you need to use QTLRel and take account of the relationships is that those relationships among individuals results in non-independence. A plot of phenotype vs genotype may appear to show a significant difference, but you can't easily account for the dependencies, in studying such a figure.

I'm not sure how you will discriminate between your two hypotheses, but I would add that it is my understanding that the F3 individuals are actually less valuable, in terms of power to detect QTL, than that number of F2s, because of the non-independence. The value of the F3s is mostly for mapping precision, due to the increased number of recombinants.

But if the F3s are showing a high degree of homozygosity, or if they're showing little variation in the phenotype, then they won't be very helpful for mapping precision, either: you need variation both in the phenotype and in the genotypes if you wish to establish an association and so map QTL.

karl

messages.author: 7409d4321b2ec671
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Problem in combining F2 with F3 generation
parts:
Dear Karl,
Thank you very much for describing in such a detail.
After I compared the scatterplots of phenotypes against genotypes of F2 and F3, I immediately understood what you meant.
It seemingly a couple of phenotypes showed F3 clusters, i.e. F3 phenotypic values are significantly different from the ones of F2, because of their high homozygosity and low phenotypic variances.
Although QTL in the other phenotypes are luckily supported by either QTL mapping with the F2 or the F3 dataset (We think we can safely say these are "real" QTL), I should keep in my mind above facts.
Anyway, Thank you very much for your comments. I really appreciate them!

Thank you.
All the best,
masato
